headlines.summary: Investing.com -- Michael Burry, the investor who famously bet against the U.S. housing market ahead of the 2008 financial crisis, has sold the remainder of his bearish Nasdaq 100 position, saying his portfolio is now temporarily almost entirely long amid heightened market volatility.

headlines.title: Prediction: This Company’s Future Could Look Very Different by the End of 2028
headlines.summary: Palantir just posted the fastest growth of its public life, and investors responded by dumping the stock for a month straight. One shaky number in the bookings data may explain the panic, and whether it deserves the fear.

headlines.title: Cathie Wood Makes a Stunning $61.6 Million Bet on a Beaten-Down AI Stock
headlines.summary: A dramatic portfolio shift reveals a different AI strategy.

headlines.title: Palantir’s CEO Alex Karp Sold $75 Million. Co-Founder Peter Thiel Bought $122 Million
headlines.summary: Palantir's two most powerful insiders moved in opposite directions on the same day, but the filings reveal that preset rules drove most of it. The real question is what Peter Thiel's timing says about a stock that swung wildly in two sessions.

news.summary: Palantir (PLTR) fell about 4.6% on November 25 amid a Nasdaq selloff that hit AI software, and the stock is reported down about 25% from its high. Insider and institutional activity was mixed that day: co-founder Peter Thiel reportedly bought $122.3 million of shares, while ARK Invest's Cathie Wood sold about $7 million. Goldman Sachs reportedly said Palantir's pilot-to-large-contract growth caught analysts' attention.
drivers: Nasdaq selloff hitting AI software stocks
Cathie Wood's ARK sale of about $7M
Goldman Sachs note on Palantir's mega-customer growth
